newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin sets crowded foreign agenda to end of year.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin sets crowded foreign agenda to end of year.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin, expected to wind up his summer vacation shortly, has a busy schedule of foreign visits to both East and West in the second half of the year, Kremlin spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky said on Wednesday.
Interfax news agency quoted Yastrzhembsky as saying that Yeltsin will first visit Strasbourg, France on October 10 and 11 to address the Council of Europe summit.
On November 10, he is due to start a visit to China, which Yastrzhembsky said would last several days. Apart from Beijing, Yeltsin also tentatively plans to travel to one of China's regions.
Yastrzhembsky said a number of economic and, possibly, arms deals were being drafted for signing during the trip.
"Yeltsin's visit is due to demonstrate the strategic nature of relations between Russia and China," he added.
On December 2 to 4 Yeltsin, who has returned to brisk activity after months of illness following his re-election last July and heart surgery in November, will pay a state visit to Sweden.
Yastrzhembsky said a number of joint economic and environmental projects will be discussed.

Yeltsin had also ordered officials to start preparing an informal meeting with Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto this year to try to develop a positive impetus in tricky bilateral relations which has started emerging lately.
"Yeltsin is very serious about the meeting," Yastrzhembsky said, adding that it could take place in Siberia or Russia's far eastern Pacific region.

Russia and Japan are at loggerheads over the South Kurile chain of islands, known in Japan as the Northern Territories, which were seized by the Soviet army at the end of World War Two. Because of the dispute, the two have yet to sign a formal post-war peace treaty.
Japan has held up major business and political deals with Russia, linking them to the return of the disputed islands.

Yastrzhembsky said that Yeltsin was expecting a number of foreign heads of state in Moscow, including talks with Turkmenistan President Saparmurat Niyazov and Armenian President Levon Ter-Petrosyan in August.
German President Roman Herzog and Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak are due to visit in September, as are Philippines President Fidel Ramos and French President Jacques Chirac.
The spokesman said Yeltsin was also planning to meet Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi, who visits Moscow in September.
